transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-23
Time: 16:00 UTC (48 minutes)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (LucidWorks, Head of ML), Aisha Grant (LucidWorks, Platform Eng), Tom Rivers (LucidWorks, CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood and LucidWorks did a kickoff to align on pilot scope for a Dedicated deployment. Discussed latency vs cost targets, network/VPC constraints, SSO, SOC 2 concerns, and benchmark plan. Agreed to run a 10M-token pilot workload, share prompt sets, and exchange documentation. Next steps and owners captured.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and success criteria
- Deployment mode: Dedicated vs hosted
- Networking and VPC peering requirements
- Security/compliance (SSO, SOC2, data retention)
- Benchmarks: latency, throughput, cost projections
- Rollout timeline and contract

Action items (auto): Ben to run bench, Maya to send pricing, customer to share network diagram.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we got 45-ish minutes on the calendar, thanks for making time. Quick intro from our side, I am Maya, AE for Redwood Inference..
[00:15] Ben Ortiz: And Ben here, SE — I'll be hands-on with the benchmark and runtime config.
[00:20] Jordan Patel: Jordan here. We're excited to get this pilot running, we have a couple of requirements around latency for search summarization workloads.
[00:30] Tom Rivers: Hi, I'm Tom, CTO. We're evaluating Dedicated because of predictable throughput and data controls.
[00:38] Aisha Grant: Aisha — platform eng. I'll own VPC and networking for the pilot.

[01:05] Maya Chen: Great — high level today: align on success criteria, agree pilot scope (model, dataset size, request QPS), confirm security checklist and plan the benchmark run. Anything urgent we should slot now?
[01:20] Jordan Patel: The big thing is p95 under 350ms for short completions (<=256 tokens) at 40 QPS per pod — that's our target, otherwise cost becomes a deal breaker.
[01:38] Ben Ortiz: OK that's helpful. One callout — p95 at 40 QPS depends a lot on batching and kv cache hit rates; do you expect a lot of repeated prefixes?
[01:50] Jordan Patel: Some repetition, yes. Search summarization does reuse prompts across users, so prefix cache may help.

[02:30] Ben Ortiz: For the Dedicated pool we can tune continuous batching, and we have quantized model profiles to reduce per-token cost. If we pick a 8-bit profile and enable prefix KV caching you often see 20-40% token cost reduction.
[02:50] Aisha Grant: Quick question on model management — will we be able to pin model versions during the pilot? We need deterministic behavior for A/B tests.
[03:05] Maya Chen: Yes, you can pin version IDs and we support canary rollouts. We'll capture that in the runbook we'll share.

[03:45] Tom Rivers: SSO and audit logs are must-haves. We need SAML SSO and audit logs retained for 1 year for compliance. Do you support that in Dedicated/private?
[03:58] Ben Ortiz: Yes, Dedicated supports SAML/SSO and audit logs. For retention beyond default we have add-ons — we'll include that in pricing.
[04:15] Jordan Patel: Also data residency — the pilot data must remain in us-east-1, no egress to other regions.
[04:25] Maya Chen: Noted — we can pin region for Dedicated.

[05:00] Aisha Grant: Networking — we plan to do VPC peering and strict firewalling. Will Redwood require outbound ports, or can we operate with minimal egress?
[05:12] Ben Ortiz: There are some control-plane callbacks for metrics and billing; for Private/VPC deployments you can opt to host the control plane inside your VPC in our Private product, but for Dedicated we'll provide a secure peering option and limited egress. We'll share a network diagram.
[05:35] Aisha Grant: FYI we run strict egress policies; we'll need the exact IP ranges and ports.

[06:10] Jordan Patel: On benchmarking — we want realistic prompts. We can share a representative set of 2000 prompts and simulate the user mix. Is 10M tokens for the pilot plausible?
[06:25] Ben Ortiz: 10M tokens with the sample prompt set is a good target; it gives stable latencies and cost estimates. We can run P0 runs for baseline and P1 runs with caching/batching tuned.
[06:40] Maya Chen: Timeline idea — share prompts by Friday (2025-06-27), Redwood runs benchmark week of 2025-06-30, debrief early July. Does that work?
[06:52] Jordan Patel: Yes.

[08:00] Tom Rivers: Pricing — are we looking at usage-based for the pilot or a small reserved commit?
[08:12] Maya Chen: For pilots we often do a short-term reserved capacity with a pilot discount so you get predictable performance. We'll send a pricing sheet and a pilot contract template.
[08:25] Tom Rivers: We also want to understand fallback policies — if Dedicated saturates, can requests fall back to hosted cheaper model so user experience stays up?
[08:39] Ben Ortiz: Yep, there are routing policies that can fallback to compatible model variants; Redwood supports automatic fallback by policy (latency vs cost). We'll demo that during the bench debrief.

[10:10] Aisha Grant: About encryption and KMS — we need server-side encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK).
[10:20] Ben Ortiz: Dedicated supports KMS integration. For Private/On-prem we have HSM integration options too.

[11:05] Jordan Patel: Anything about evals? We want quality regressions to be caught; we have evaluation harnesses.
[11:15] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set regressions and send alerts if quality drops. For pilot we'll run baseline evals and tie them to the alert thresholds you define.

[12:00] Tom Rivers: Can you send the security pack — SOC 2, ISO, pen test report? We'll send to our procurement team.
[12:12] Maya Chen: Absolutely — I'll include the link to our security whitepaper and SOC 2 summary in the follow-up email.

[13:30] Jordan Patel: On model selection — we were eyeing an open Llama-style variant and one higher-quality transformer for the A/B. Will Redwood host both?
[13:45] Ben Ortiz: Yes, we can host multiple model variants and handle routing. Some model names sometimes get transcribed wrong in auto-exports — but we'll list exact model IDs in the runbook.

[15:00] Aisha Grant: A practical: what metrics will you report after bench? We need P50/P95 latency, token cost, throughput, GPU utilization?
[15:12] Ben Ortiz: We'll provide P50/P95, tail-latency histograms, cost per 1k tokens, and GPU util percent. Also per-route breakdowns so you can see where cache helps.

[17:05] Jordan Patel: Any gotchas with prefix caching vs user isolation? We have multi-tenant concerns.
[17:18] Ben Ortiz: Prefix/KV cache is opt-in per route; for multi-tenant you can scope cache per-tenant or per-route. We'll go over best practices in the runbook.

[18:40] Maya Chen: Quick recap and responsibilities: Maya will send pricing/security docs; Ben runs bench; LucidWorks provides prompt set and network diagram. Any additions?
[18:55] Tom Rivers: Can we lock a demo of the console and tracing for our infra team? They want to see per-token cost breakdown and traces.
[19:08] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll schedule a console walkthrough after the bench.

[20:30] Jordan Patel: Onboarding support — do you provide a CSM during pilot or only for Dedicated contracts?
[20:42] Maya Chen: For pilots we assign a CSM for the duration; they'll help with runbook and rollout. For enterprise Dedicated there's a dedicated success team.

[22:00] Aisha Grant: One more networking detail: we will test with strict MTLS; is that supported?
[22:12] Ben Ortiz: Yes, mTLS for transport is supported on Dedicated, we'll include config snippets.

[25:00] (brief cross-talk about calendar availability and scheduling)

[28:45] Ben Ortiz: I'll put together the benchmark plan: workload shape, QPS ramps, cache on/off, quant profiles. We'll run baseline then optimized.
[29:00] Jordan Patel: Please include a cost projection table — industry wants to see token cost delta across profiles.

[32:10] Tom Rivers: Procurement will need a short SOW for the pilot. Maya, can you send a contract stub we can hand to legal?
[32:22] Maya Chen: Yes — pilot contract template and SOW stub in follow-up.

[34:00] Jordan Patel: If bench results look good we want to fold this into a 6-month reserved capacity.
[34:10] Maya Chen: Sounds good — we'll include options in the pricing package.

[36:00] (short technical aside about kernel selection and sequence length impacts; Ben gives a quick explainer)
[37:20] Ben Ortiz: Longer sequences change kernel selection and memory profile; for short summarization workloads you can pick optimized kernels.
[37:40] Aisha Grant: We'll share representative sequence length distribution with you.

[40:00] Maya Chen: Alright, last bit — risks and blockers? Anything we need to unblock immediately?
[40:12] Aisha Grant: IP and security review by our procurement team — they'll want SOC 2 and SSO details, plus the network ranges.
[40:25] Tom Rivers: Budget approval might be delayed but pilot-level reserve is usually fast.

[42:00] Maya Chen: OK recap of next steps — I'll email pricing, security docs, pilot SOW; Ben will schedule the bench and share plan; Jordan/Aisha provide prompt set and network diagram. We'll aim for bench week of 2025-06-30 and debrief first week of July.
[42:25] Jordan Patel: Great.
[43:00] Tom Rivers: Thanks everyone.
[47:30] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with links and dates. Bye.

End of transcript.
